title: Some questions no program can answer

probes.question: What does the halting problem ask?
options: Whether a program will finish or run forever

probes.question: True or false: Turing proved that one algorithm can decide the halting problem for every program and input.

image.alt: A dark slate sculpture of Alan Turing seated at a desk, made by Stephen Kettle and shown in a museum.

body.claim: No single program can tell, for every other program, whether it will finish or run forever.
body.why: This is the halting problem: given a program and an input, decide whether it eventually halts or runs forever. Alan Turing proved in 1937 that no general algorithm can solve it for all program-input pairs. A proof by contradiction supposes such a checker exists and shows that leads to nonsense.
